content.title: About
content.content: Greek yogurt made from whole milk is a thick, creamy yogurt obtained by extensive straining, which removes most of the whey. It has a rich, buttery flavor with a mild tang and a high protein content.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Greek yogurt, known as “straggisto” in Greece, has been a staple of the Mediterranean diet for centuries.
Straining makes it 2‑3 times thicker than regular yogurt.
Its high protein level makes it popular among athletes and fitness enthusiasts.
Unlike low‑fat versions, the whole‑milk product retains natural fats that aid absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins.
Greek yogurt is often used as a substitute for sour cream or mayonnaise in recipes.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: A typical 200 g serving provides about 10‑12 g of high‑quality protein, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Contains live cultures of Lactobacillus and Bifidobacterium that promote a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Whole milk supplies a good amount of calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Provides vitamin B12 and riboflavin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Satiety aid
items.content: The thick texture and protein content help keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Although some lactose is removed during straining, the product still contains enough to cause symptoms in lactose‑intolerant individuals.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People allergic to casein or whey proteins may react to Greek yogurt.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Whole‑milk Greek yogurt contains roughly 120 kcal per 100 g, so portion control is advisable for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some brands add salt; those monitoring sodium intake should check the label.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy it plain, blend into smoothies, use as a base for dips and dressings, or substitute for cream cheese in baking and cooking.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated at +2‑4 °C in the original container. Once opened, consume within 5‑7 days. Discard if it develops off‑odors, mold, or an unusual texture.
